segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Then the kingdom of the heavens will be like ten young women who took their torches and went out to meet the bridegroom.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Five of them were foolish and five were sensible.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For the foolish ones, when they took their torches, took no oil with them;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but the sensible ones took oil in flasks along with their torches.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As the bridegroom was a long time coming, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But in the middle of the night there was a shout: ‘Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then all those young women got up and put their torches in order.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The foolish ones said to the sensible, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our torches are going out.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the sensible ones answered, ‘No, there may not be enough for us and for you. Go instead to the dealers and buy some for yourselves.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: While they were going off to buy it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Later the rest of the young women came as well, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open the door for us!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But he answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So stay awake, because you do not know the day or the hour.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “For it is like a man going abroad, who called his own slaves and handed his property over to them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, each according to his own ability, and he went abroad. At once

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the one who had received the five talents went and put them to work and gained five more.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In the same way the one with the two gained two more.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the one who had received the one went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “After a long time the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one who had received the five talents came forward and brought five more talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed five talents over to me; see, I have gained five more talents.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few things; I will put you in charge of many. Enter into your master’s joy.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one with the two talents also came forward and said, ‘Master, you handed two talents over to me; see, I have gained two more talents.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few things; I will put you in charge of many. Enter into your master’s joy.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then the one who had received the one talent also came forward and said, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: so I was afraid, and I went off and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what is yours.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But his master answered him, ‘You wicked and lazy slave! You knew, did you, that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received what was mine with interest.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have more than enough; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And throw the useless slave out into the outer darkness. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and he will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then the king will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me a drink, I was a stranger and you took me in,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did it for me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Then he will also say to those on his left, ‘Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I was hungry and you did not give me anything to eat, I was thirsty and you did not give me a drink,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I was a stranger and you did not take me in, naked and you did not clothe me, sick and in prison and you did not look after me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve you?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then he will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it for me either.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

notes.note: The Greek is plural, a Semitic turn of phrase characteristic of Matthew, and this translation keeps it. Most English versions flatten it to 'heaven'. The meaning is the same: God's reign.

The Greek word denotes a girl or young woman of marriageable age who is not yet married. Virginity is assumed but is not the point of the story, and 'virgins' puts the emphasis in the wrong place for a modern reader. Most translations keep 'virgins'; some have 'bridesmaids', which fits their role here but is more specific than the Greek.

The ordinary Greek word for a household oil lamp is a different one (lychnos). The word used here normally means a torch, and many commentators picture sticks wrapped in oil-soaked cloth carried in a night-time wedding procession. Most translations have 'lamps', and the word can occasionally bear that meaning; the oil and the 'going out' fit either. The question is not settled.
The Greek word denotes practical good sense and foresight, not wisdom in the larger sense, for which Greek has another word. Most translations have 'wise'; some have 'prudent'.

The Greek word means a slave, a person owned by a master, not a hired servant. Slaves in the ancient world could be entrusted with managing large sums and running businesses on their owner's behalf, which is the situation the parable assumes. Many older translations soften the word to 'servants'; a number of recent ones use 'slaves'.

A talent was a unit of weight and, as money, a very large sum of silver: about six thousand denarii, something like twenty years' wages for a labourer. The English sense of 'talent' as a natural ability arose from this parable and is not part of the Greek word's meaning.

The Greek word for 'at once' stands at the end of verse 15 and can be read with what precedes (the man left at once) or with what follows (the first slave went to work at once). The punctuation of the Greek edition translated here, and most modern translations, take it with the slave's action; older versions took it with the departure.

The Greek word is the same one rendered 'Gentiles' elsewhere in this translation; in the plural it can mean the peoples of the world or specifically the non-Jewish peoples. Most interpreters take the scene as a judgment of all humanity, but some argue that only the nations outside Israel, or outside the church, are in view. The 'them' who are separated is grammatically masculine, indicating individual people and not nations as units.

The Greek verb means to go to see someone in order to help, and regularly carries the sense of caring for them. 'Visited', the traditional rendering, suggests a social call to a modern reader. Several modern translations render it 'looked after' or 'took care of'.

notes.phrase: the least of these brothers and sisters of mine
notes.traditional: the least of these my brethren
notes.note: The Greek plural 'brothers' includes women as well as men. Who is meant is disputed. Elsewhere in Matthew, Jesus calls his disciples his brothers (12:49–50; 28:10) and promises reward to anyone who gives them a cup of water (10:42), so many scholars take the phrase to mean his followers, perhaps his travelling messengers. The long-standing and widely held alternative is that it means any person in need. The translation leaves the question open, as the Greek does.

The Greek adjective is formed from the word for 'age'. In Jewish usage of the period it describes what belongs to the age to come, so that 'eternal life' (verse 46) is the life of that age, a matter of kind as well as of length. 'Eternal' is the standard rendering and is kept here; a minority of translators render 'of the age to come'. The same word qualifies fire, punishment and life in verses 41 and 46.

candidates.reason: Occurs throughout the New Testament and translations split between 'slave' and 'servant', including in Paul's self-descriptions, so one policy is needed.
Jesus' formula 'Amen, I say to you' recurs across all four Gospels and is variously rendered 'truly', 'amen', 'I assure you'; readers should see one form.
The plural is used very frequently for mixed groups of believers, and whether to render 'brothers' or 'brothers and sisters' should be decided once.
The choice between 'virgin' and 'young (unmarried) woman' matters at Matthew 1:23, Luke 1:27 and 1 Corinthians 7, and needs a sense-by-sense ruling.
Recurs in the Gospels and Paul and is usually rendered 'wise', which blurs it with σοφός; a consistent distinction would help readers.
